newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rampant UCB boosts Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Rampant UCB boosts Brussels bourse.

text.p: Belgian pharmaceutical star UCB, up more than 10 percent on strongly positive comments from Tuesday's annual meeting, boosted the Brussels bourse to new highs on Wednesday despite a spate of shares going ex-dividend.
"UCB is the pillar holding up the market this morning," one trader said. "Technically the index should have dropped about 17 points gross on the dividend payments."
The share was up 10.4 percent at 111,300 francs at 0940 GMT having earlier hit a new high of 114,000 francs.
The Bel-20 index was 11.09 points or 0.47 percent higher at 2,363.24 after hitting a new intra-day high of 2,371.02 .BFX.

On Tuesday UCB reported a strong performance in the United States for its anti-allergy drug Zyrtec, said it hoped to issue it on the Japanese market next year, spoke of "very favourable" performances in all its three sectors and mentioned a possible share split to make the shares more accessible.
The share's remarkable leap higher on Wednesday was the key but not the sole motor behind the market's general ascension.

"All the fundamentals are still positive. There is no reason to see any weakness in coming days, although we are keeping a close eye on those fundamentals just in case they start to turn against us," one trader said.
"Everything looks bright. Interest rates are low, the dollar is positive and there is a lot of liquidity looking for an investment," said another trader.
Almanij, Ackermans, Bekaert, Brederode, D'Ieteren, Finoutremer, Fortis AG, Glaverbel, Koramic, Royale Belge, Solvay, Spector, Telinfo and Tractebel all go ex-dividend today.
But such was the strength of the market that most shares had recovered some or all of their initial losses by late morning, traders noted.
